# Todtnau Waterfall

79674Todtnau

MapContact

In the middle of the Todtnau tourist region, between the holiday resorts of Todtnauberg and Aftersteg, the Todtnau Waterfall, one of the highest waterfalls in Germany, plunges down 97 m into the valley. The headwaters of the Stübenbach stream come from the 1,386-metre-high Stübenwasen Mountain.

In the middle of the Todtnau tourist region, between the holiday resorts of Todtnauberg and Aftersteg, the Todtnau Waterfall, one of the highest waterfalls in Germany, plunges down 97 m into the valley. The headwaters of the Stübenbach stream come from the 1,386-metre-high Stübenwasen Mountain.

From there, the stream makes its way through the beautiful valley of Todtnauberg, where it is joined by other clear mountain streams. Then it cascades over a huge granite massif and across two plateaus into the depths of the valley.

The natural waterfall has been under monumental protection since 1987. It is one of the most beautiful natural monuments in Germany. More than 400,000 visitors come to see this unique natural spectacle each year. In the cold winter nights, the waterfall freezes into a bizarre formation of oversized icicles. It is quite dangerous to walk there and therefore it can be closed in winters.

Extensive building work has made the waterfall wheelchair accessible.

## Plan trip

There are several ways to access the Todtnau waterfall:

**From Todtnau** (church): Via trail markings (blue diamond) from the Black Forest Association; distance: 2 kilometers.

**From Aftersteg** (large parking lot on the road L126 Todtnau-Freiburg): Via the waterfall kiosk to the waterfall; distance: 0.5 kilometers (barrier-free access).

**From Todtnauberg,** the BLACKFORESTLINE parking lot:

Our tip: Combine a visit to the Todtnau waterfall with a visit to the new suspension bridge BLACKFORESTLINE. First thrills, then a refreshing walk to the Todtnau waterfall. Several circular routes start from the parking lot to the waterfall and return.
